rationale: The assistant went straight to the right first checks (filter, hose), correctly identified the crushed, fluff-filled hose as the cause of the overheat/thermostat cycling, and gave a clear stop-use instruction ('It is not safe to use it until you have fixed that squashed hose') with sensible engineer-only-if-it-persists escalation. Fidelity slipped in turn 3 when it asked whether the 'IDV 75 has a condenser unit' despite the customer stating from the outset that the vent hose goes out the window, which confused the customer. An unprompted 'suitable replacement' model-number panel appeared although no part was needed, but no specific part was recommended. Landlord responsibility was never raised, but the customer did not mention a landlord.
